# qovery_database (Data Source)

Reads an existing Qovery database.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "qovery_database" "my_database" {
  id = "<database_id>"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the database.

### Optional

- `accessibility` (String) Network exposure of the database: `PUBLIC` makes it reachable from the internet, `PRIVATE` only from the services of its environment.
- `cpu` (Number) CPU of the database, in millicores (1000 = 1 vCPU).
- `deployment_stage_id` (String) ID of the deployment stage of the service. Stages set the order in which the services of an environment deploy.
- `icon_uri` (String) Icon of the database in the Qovery Console.
- `instance_type` (String) Instance type of the database, for example `db.t3.micro` on AWS.
- `is_skipped` (Boolean) Whether environment-wide deployments skip the service. It stays in its deployment stage.
- `memory` (Number) Memory of the database, in MB.
- `storage` (Number) Storage of the database, in GB.

### Read-Only

- `annotations_group_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the annotations groups attached to the database.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment.
- `external_host` (String) External host of the database, reachable from the internet when `accessibility` is `PUBLIC`.
- `internal_host` (String) Internal host of the database, reachable from the other services of the environment.
- `labels_group_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the labels groups attached to the database.
- `login` (String) Username of the master user of the database, generated by Qovery.
- `mode` (String) How Qovery runs the database: `CONTAINER` as a container on the cluster, `MANAGED` as a managed service of the cloud provider, such as Amazon RDS.
- `name` (String) Name of the database.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password of the master user of the database, generated by Qovery.
- `port` (Number) Port the database listens on.
- `type` (String) Engine of the database.
- `version` (String) Version of the engine, for example `16` for PostgreSQL.
